videos.title: 2026 in LLMs — Simon Willison, Datasette
videos.summary: Delivered as a brilliant, deadpan speculative keynote from late 2026, Simon Willison maps out the near future of agentic AI across three major inflection points—from autonomous brute-force problem solvers to AI-designed games. His core payoff reveals the developer's ultimate paradox: AI doesn't replace software engineers or make work easier, but by automating routine tasks in seconds, it forces us to tackle far more complex, ambitious problems at breakneck speed. Though framed through a playful sci-fi lens featuring fictional future models, this talk offers an indispensable reality check on where agentic technology is genuinely headed.

timestamps.topic: The 'Fable-class' model shift and brute-force real-world problem solving
Testing whether autonomous AI can understand 'fun' and design games
The engineering paradox: why AI makes software development harder, not easier

videos.title: New Ways of Working with Codex — Dominik Kundel & Charlie Guo, OpenAI
videos.summary: Imagine stepping into the near future where you stop micromanaging code and instead orchestrate a fleet of autonomous background agents using your voice like Tony Stark. Presented as a visionary dispatch framed from the year 2026, OpenAI developers showcase a radical leap in developer workflow—replacing tedious prompt engineering with self-configuring multi-repo cloud VMs, live interactive UI prototyping, and multi-agent delegation. It is an indispensable blueprint for anyone wanting to see the cutting edge of AI-native software engineering and harness long-running autonomous workflows today.

timestamps.topic: Rapid UI iteration and live interactive prototyping
Autonomous multi-repo cloud development environments
Using voice mode as an agentic control plane across apps

videos.title: Let's Open Source the World — Brandon Thomas, ArtCraft
videos.summary: What if autonomous AI agents could rebuild bloated, multi-billion-dollar software monopolies like Photoshop and Figma practically overnight? In this audacious presentation framed as a dispatch from the future (dated November 2026), Brandon Thomas reveals how autonomous code generation and Rust could dismantle closed SaaS ecosystems—though viewers must maintain healthy skepticism, as his sensational claims of overnight full-suite clones and millions of daily users serve as a speculative thought experiment rather than current reality. It is a must-watch blueprint for anyone seeking to understand how agentic factories could soon disrupt proprietary software and return digital ownership to creators.

timestamps.topic: The 'enshittification' trap: How open protocols were replaced by extractive corporate platforms
Agentic reverse-engineering: Rebuilding Photoshop and desktop creative suites with AI
Autonomous software factories: Where AI agents excel versus where human design is required

videos.title: If You Have a Job, Start Selling Your Skills ASAP
videos.summary: No matter how talented you are, your salary will always hit a hard ceiling if you only focus on doing the work rather than learning how to win it. This video reveals the counterintuitive reality that clients never pay for technical skills—only the specific problems those skills solve—and breaks down the exact framework to multiply your earning power without dancing on social media or quitting your day job. Watch this to avoid the devastating trap of spending months creating courses or apps before climbing the proven 'leverage ladder.'

timestamps.topic: The Salary Ceiling: Why winning work pays dramatically more than doing it

The Leverage Ladder: Scaling your service and avoiding the passive income trap
